target_customer: Women buying, renting or selling formalwear (prom, pageant and event gowns)
problem: Formalwear is worn once and expensive; buyers struggle to find and afford dresses and sellers have no good resale channel.
business_model: Marketplace take rate on peer-to-peer formalwear sales and rentals (iOS, Android, web)

founders.name: Trisha Bantigue
founders.background_notes: Forbes 30 Under 30 2022 (Art & Style); YC says her inspiration was her own struggle to find and afford a dress.

founders.name: Kathy Zhou-Patel
education: University of Pennsylvania, BA Computer Science and Environmental Science (2015)

technical_complexity.rationale: Standard marketplace with mobile apps; the hard parts were logistics and supply, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Supply and demand liquidity in a niche, but resale marketplaces for fashion were copyable and no data on its share was found.

market_need_then: Own site claims it is the leading marketplace for formalwear; YC bio cites founder experience of unaffordable dresses. No independent spend data seen.

branding.domain_note: queenly.com was the company domain; it now 301-redirects to gritbrokerage.com, a domain broker (checked November 2026).

identity.voice_and_tone: Empowering ('make every woman look and feel like a queen', own copy)

brand_strength.rationale: Evocative pageant-aligned name with a clear mission line and Forbes recognition, but nothing shows community or virality.

outcome_analysis: Queenly is listed Inactive by YC and its queenly.com domain now redirects to a domain broker, which suggests the product ended, but no shutdown notice, acquisition or post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public in the sources reached. The company reached 13 people and claimed backing from a16z, NextView and The House Fund and a Forbes feature in 2022, so it was not a trivial failure, but without a stated reason no failure factors are recorded.
